analysis.title: More thoughts on the post-midterm policy outlook
key_insights: Despite a comprehensive Democratic win in the 2026 midterms, with larger-than-anticipated majorities in both chambers, CACIB's base case is still legislative gridlock in Washington. That leaves no scope for large-scale progressive action and limited room for major fiscal packages.

Democrats are expected to push targeted proposals where compromise looks possible. The likely priorities are rolling back a subset of Trump's tariffs, reversing Medicaid cuts in the OBBBA, and restoring the enhanced ACA tax credits that expired.

The debt ceiling is Democrats' main point of leverage. The US last raised it in 2025 to $41.1trn, and the Bipartisan Policy Centre projects federal debt will hit the limit between late winter and mid-summer 2027. Extraordinary measures would push the x-date out another six to nine months.
A government shutdown fight is a second source of leverage, but a weaker one than the debt ceiling because a shutdown is less consequential than a default.

Republicans could in theory extend government funding and raise the debt ceiling before the new Congress takes office on 3 January, which would delay Democratic leverage. Current funding expires 11 December. A fractured Republican caucus makes anything beyond a short-term continuing resolution uncertain.

Tariffs: CACIB does not expect Democrats to try to overturn all of Trump's tariffs. It thinks they would target a subset, possibly tariffs on Canada or broader North American tariffs as the USMCA renegotiation proceeds.

Congress could theoretically retake delegated tariff powers if enough Republicans defect, but overriding a veto needs two-thirds majorities in both chambers. CACIB does not treat this as its base case.

Medicaid: the OBBBA cuts roughly $1trn of spending over 10 years, mainly through work requirements of at least 80 hours a month for non-disabled adults. Medicaid spending is still projected to grow, only more slowly.

Iran war: Schumer has pledged to 'end the war'. CACIB is sceptical because Trump can veto a War Powers Resolution and conduct much foreign policy without Congress. A veto override needs two-thirds majorities in both chambers.
A second route for Democrats is the power of the purse. Blocking new Pentagon funding is easier than blocking funds already appropriated, which the Defense Department can sometimes repurpose.

Trump's recent rhetoric on Iran has sounded more conciliatory, and the midterm defeat may push him to pull back. CACIB still sees a behavioural risk that he lashes out in areas where he can act without Congress, including re-escalation in Iran.

AI: CACIB is sceptical that major restrictions will come from Washington because Trump is staunchly pro-AI and can veto aggressive regulation. AI-hostile Democratic governors who won key states could slow data centre construction or push projects to other states, delaying but not derailing the buildout.

sector_views.rationale: The AI buildout could be slowed by state and local roadblocks, such as data centre construction delays and project relocations, but is unlikely to be derailed. Federal restrictions are unlikely because of Trump's veto.
Democrats are expected to try to reverse OBBBA Medicaid cuts and restore enhanced ACA tax credits. Gridlock and the presidential veto make passage uncertain.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Debt is projected to reach the limit between late winter and mid-summer 2027, with extraordinary measures adding six to nine months. Democrats could use the required increase as leverage.
The estimated reduction in spending growth is a likely Democratic target for reversal.

geopolitical: Iran war: Schumer pledged to 'end the war', but Trump's veto and foreign policy powers limit what Congress can do, and he could re-escalate.
USMCA renegotiation is in progress and could be a focus for rolling back tariffs on Canada or North America.
Democrats may try a War Powers Resolution or blocking Pentagon funding to constrain the Iran war.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats use the debt ceiling and a possible shutdown as leverage to extract targeted concessions on tariffs, Medicaid and ACA tax credits.
tension_points.bear_case: The filibuster and presidential veto block most proposals, and Republicans could pass longer-term funding plus a debt ceiling increase before 3 January, which would delay Democratic leverage.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Republicans agree on longer-term funding and a debt ceiling increase before the new Congress takes office on 3 January, or enough Republicans defect to reach veto-proof two-thirds majorities.

tension_points.bull_case: Democrats could end the war through a War Powers Resolution or by blocking new Pentagon funding, and Trump may pull back on his own given the war's unpopularity.
tension_points.bear_case: Trump can veto a War Powers Resolution, already appropriated funds can be repurposed, and he could re-escalate where he can act without Congress.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Enough Republicans join Democrats to gain two-thirds majorities in both chambers to override a veto.

theme_stances.key_argument: Despite larger Democratic majorities, the filibuster and presidential veto mean the base case is gridlock, with only targeted compromises possible.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to expect a base case that largely involves legislative gridlock

theme_stances.key_argument: Washington is unlikely to impose major AI restrictions because of Trump's veto, but Democratic governors could slow data centre construction.
theme_stances.evidence: the AI buildout could be slowed a bit, but is unlikely to be entirely derailed
